context:
This item asks you to lift a limit in a recorded ruling. It does not block anything.
Goal: fewer repeat lane lints after main moves (your 23:04 CST Nov 14 words, "850 a").
Problem (rule): ruling own-850-a lets the lane lint carry across a clean merge of main, in the form the merge tool proves, and nothing else. A claim commit or a page commit made after a clean merge does not carry the lint. Decision lanes-run-no-full-ci-job (PR 3481) says so, citing that ruling. Lifting the limit needs your word, and it changes what a lint pass covers.
Based on (ruling): own-850-a, your pick a, saved 23:04 CST Nov 14. It reads: "Not covered: a merge with any other change, a conflict-resolved merge, a merge whose tree differs from git's own merge, an unreadable merge-tree (reads unknown, not carried), or any other lint-carried form." A claim or page commit after the merge is such an other form.
Based on (read): the review-carries lane, 02:40 CST Nov 15, relayed by the coordinator at 02:41 CST: its tests test_b_a_claim_after_a_clean_merge_is_not_carried and test_b_a_records_page_after_a_clean_merge_is_not_carried assert the current rule.
Based on (unmeasured): how often this costs a re-lint. Your own number for the clean-merge case was 6 lints and 56 min in one evening (runner 10's read, unverified by triage); nobody has counted the claim-or-page case.
Departs from: ruling own-850-a — adds a carry for a claim or page commit made after a clean merge of main, which that ruling leaves out.
Who recommends what: the coordinator recommends keeping the limit (option b) until the cost is measured.
Meanwhile: lane review-carries builds without this. Its next PR builds only the no-stamp page carry (step lint-carries-page-commit-no-stamp), which stays inside own-850-a's proved form.
home: ruling own-850-a-lane-lint-carries-clean-main-merge; steps carry-forgives-main-merge and lint-carries-page-commit-no-stamp; decision lanes-run-no-full-ci-job (PR 3481)

options.gain: Fewer repeat lane lints after main moves.
options.how: The merge tool and lane lint also accept the earlier lint pass after a claim or page commit that follows a clean merge. The two tests that assert the current rule are re-pointed.
options.label: Lift the limit: carry the lane lint across a claim or page commit made after a clean merge
options.lose: A lint pass then covers a tree it never ran on, in a wider form than the one you accepted; two tests re-point; a page commit made before the merge needs its own ruling. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo, if the carry widens the tool beyond the proved form.

options.gain: The proved form stays exact; no test changes.
options.how: No change. A claim or page commit after a clean merge still gets a new lane lint. The cost is measured first, then you are asked again if it is high.
options.label: Keep the limit: carry only across a clean merge, as own-850-a says (recommended by the coordinator)
options.lose: A lane re-lints after a claim or page commit that follows a clean merge (8 to 12 min each, your own number for the clean-merge case; unmeasured here).
